applies_why: This text decides a challenge to a dropped limb, not a chain-against-chain collision over a live link, so K-C does not govern it.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Jeremiah 22:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: witnesses pressed against a link: I read 'link' as a live link still being defended, while the other reading would apply K-C to a limb already dropped; under the live-link reading there is no collision to weigh.
why: The judge treats the challenge as moot because the targeted limb was dropped, not by applying the retired stating-verse test, so it does not violate K-C.
